title: Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane farmers hits Belagavi, but neighbouring districts unaffected

ai.summary: Karnataka sugarcane farmers called a bandh on October 31 demanding ₹5,500 per tonne, halting activities in Belagavi district towns but affecting only local areas with no impact in neighboring districts.

facts.claim: Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane growers who are demanding a price of ₹5,500 per tonne
facts.quote: Normal activities came to a halt in several towns and hobli centres in Belagavi district on October 31 in response to the Karnataka bandh called by sugarcane growers who are demanding a price of ₹5,500 per tonne.

facts.claim: Protesting farmers briefly prevented buses from leaving the Central Bus Stand in Belagavi
facts.quote: Protesting farmers briefly prevented buses from leaving the Central Bus Stand in Belagavi.

facts.claim: A scuffle broke out between the protesters and the police when the latter attempted to stop them
facts.quote: A scuffle broke out between the protesters and the police when the latter attempted to stop them.

facts.claim: Several shops were reportedly closed during the protest
facts.quote: Several shops were reportedly closed during the protest.

facts.claim: Commercial activity remained largely suspended in Hukkeri, Raibag, Mudalagi, Athani, Nipani, and Chikkodi taluk headquarters
facts.quote: Commercial activity remained largely suspended in Hukkeri, Raibag, Mudalagi, Athani, Nipani, and Chikkodi taluk headquarters

facts.claim: Farmers blocked roads at several locations across the district as part of the protest
facts.quote: Farmers blocked roads at several locations across the district as part of the protest.

facts.claim: In Dharwad, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Haveri, and Gadag districts, the protests were largely symbolic
facts.quote: In Dharwad, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Haveri, and Gadag districts, the protests were largely symbolic.

facts.claim: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to sugarcane farmers protesting over prices to abide by the understanding reached at the meeting on October 26
facts.quote: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed to sugarcane farmers protesting over prices to abide by the understanding reached at the meeting on October 26.

facts.claim: Sugar factories cannot afford higher procurement prices without a revision in sugar price by the Union Government
facts.quote: Mr. Shivakumar said that sugar factories cannot afford higher procurement prices without a revision in sugar price by the Union Government.

facts.claim: The Centre should increase the price of sugar to at least ₹50 a kg
facts.quote: The Chief Minister reiterated that the Centre should increase the price of sugar to at least ₹50 a kg

ai.background_note: Karnataka sugarcane farmers demanded ₹5,500 per tonne after state offered ₹3,300, leading to a localized bandh in Belagavi district on October 31, 2026.
